**Conversation Overview**

This conversation consists entirely of Claude executing a highly structured, protocol-driven technical workflow called "Phase R2" — a systematic line-by-line reading and verification of a large academic text called "The Method 1.6." The person uploaded a handoff document (HANDOFF-73.md) and issued a single instruction: "Continue." Claude then autonomously completed an entire work segment spanning gate verification, section reading, instrumentation, build construction, and handoff writing for the next session.

The workflow follows an elaborate multi-step protocol: Claude fetches two Google Drive bundles (BUILD90 main and BUILD150 compendia), verifies cryptographic checksums (md5), extracts member files, runs gate verification instruments, reads a designated section of the main volume (L8889–L9029, covering sections §32.1.2 through §32.1.4.1, 141 lines), writes two Python instrument batches (computable and prose), banks their outputs as goldens, records deviations and verified findings in a READ file, builds a new bundle (BUILD150), and writes a detailed handoff document for the next chat session (HANDOFF-74). The main volume is now 76.1% read at L9029 of 11,855 lines.

The session identified eight deviations in the text under review (labeled 16o-01 through 16o-08), including a stale baseline computation, arithmetically impossible table row sums, mismatched index counts, an incorrect size comparison, a companion paper count discrepancy, a pointer to a section that does not contain the attributed claim, a corrupt duplicated sentence, and superseded audit counts printed without state markers. Twenty-one verified findings confirmed correct mathematics and prose. Six instrument faults were self-caught and corrected in place. The close produced READ-ch16o.md, CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch16o.tsv, W-160, DEF-121, BUILD150, and HANDOFF-74.

**Tool Knowledge**

Google Drive downloads in this workflow use `Google Drive:search_files` with `title contains 'BUILD150_compendia' or title contains 'BUILD90_main'` and `excludeContentSnippets: True`, then `Google Drive:download_file_content` by fileId. The resulting spill files land at `/mnt/user-data/tool_results/<toolu_id>.json` and must be decoded via `json.loads(json.load(open(spill))[0]['text'])['content']` before base64 decoding. The Prints & Proofs original has a stable fileId (`1vsWwRT9BmUNeMrqokuo4jI4DJnoADubH`) and must be fetched separately and written to `/home/claude/PP_The_Method_1_6.md`. All gate steps use `timeout 280` on every bash call. The `gate.py manifest` step reports FAIL on changed members after a close because extracted copies stay at pre-close state; appends must be verified by reading the new bundle directly rather than relying on manifest output.

## Chat 121 — position report

**Gate: PASS.** All nine steps in order. BUILD90 main (49065309…, 18,470 lines) and BUILD149 compendia (64ff9011…, 89,677 lines, 546 members extracted), Prints & Proofs original (49900cf4…, 11,371 lines) fetched, census byte-identical, five core instruments OK, MANIFEST OK, chat 120's two goldens reproduced, GATE-ch121 written.

**Unit cut: L8889–L9029, 141 lines** — §32.1.2 through §32.1.4.1, the whole movement, closing where §32.2 begins. Re-measured by my own heading scan; every heading matched the handoff. Read in full, censused, both instrument batches run and **banked** (r2-ch16m 11,481 B, r2-ch16n 19,953 B). Main volume now **76.1 % read (L9029 of 11,855)**.

**The mathematics is exact and it is the largest verified block of the phase.** All five rows of the enlargement table reproduce exactly — 976, 8,853, 89,438, 267,858, 499,246 — and |ℛ(Λ)| = |Λ| with E = 0 measured at the first three; the last two are a stated budget bound, not a negative. Register 236 carries the same figures at its headline. The 55 cells sum exactly, the recomputed 48 reproduces exactly (4 + 4 + 23 + 17), 18/68 = 26 % under all three conventions, 26/4 = 6.5, the fivefold rise is exact, all twenty cited registers exist and are on point, and Λ's four figures hold across all three states while the book's three move — §32.1.4.1's own claim, verified row by row.

**Deviations that carry.** A 4 % baseline computed over twenty-five chapters where the volume has thirty-six — the same stale-self-measurement class as chat 120's 16m-01, except here it *understates* the book's own result (the true multiple is 9.5×, not 6.5×). Two of the three rows of §32.1.3's table sum to 98, which three rounded percentages of a partition cannot do. "Six indices" over five distinct indices named, and "only two closed" matching neither the fibred reading (three) nor the section's own honest-number rule (one). "The register is a quarter of it" measured at 35.8 % by lines and 60.8 % by bytes. "The two companion papers" against the volume's own "third companion paper" at two sites. §22.4 cited for a closing result about language when §22.4 is the price of limit-freedom, and "no language for" occurs nowhere else in the volume. And a spliced line at L8910 printing "= 0 at one fibre = 0 at one fibre", with Appendix D's 4 attached to the fibred reading its own table gives as 0.

**Chat 120's live thread is closed as a pass.** §32.1.1's ten bolded items are three ordinals plus seven numbered; §32.1.2 answers 1, 2, 4, 6 and defers 3, 5, 7 — exactly the seven numbered, no gap. The title is right; only §32.1.1's two labelling conventions are at fault.

**Also recorded on the positive side:** Ruling 46 clean (zero sites), no attributions to bibliograph, 95 long lines with zero recurrence (fifteen consecutive clean units), the two census rows in range both C9 artefacts on the section's own claims, §18.6 and §12.11.3.1 exact at their targets, §17.2 read in full and carrying the substance L8991 attributes to it, all part labels resolving, and the entire unit present in Prints & Proofs at a uniform −94 — authored before this build, not at it. Ruling 45 sites: twelve in 141 lines, chapter 32 still the densest region.

**Six instrument faults, all self-caught and rewritten in place, none trimmed** — a dash-only grouped-heading pattern that saw none of the Register's seven comma-grouped headings; a §7.4 probe that returned nothing without stating its coverage; a case-sensitive PP witness scoring zero on its own volume; a join that broke on the body indent; a lookbehind hiding sentence-initial attributions; and one protocol fault of my own, chaining the pycache delete to a gate call against G0e.

**Not done.** The close is unbuilt: READ-ch16o.md, CENSUS-CLOSURES-ch16o.tsv, W-160, DEF-121, BUILD150, HANDOFF-74 all remain, and I hit the tool limit with both goldens banked but nothing written. The section read itself is complete and closed — nothing is half-measured — but the segment cannot be declared closed until the build exists. Say "continue" and I will write all six and build BUILD150 in the next response.

- The review plan: R1 instrumented census → **R2 full read in source order (in progress: next §12.11.1.1, main L3177)** → R3 corrections by class → R4 cross-volume audit. Then the compendium task line: renumber → bibliography → Register expansions → main-volume prose.
- Governing members (read at every open): `RULINGS-R2.md` (rulings, append-only), `DEFERRED.md` (cross-chapter items, append-only; do not re-derive), the READ-chNN.md members and W-101… in WORKING-REGISTER.md (findings; never restated in handoffs).

## 4. Rulings in force

- Chat 67: every volume read in full, no editing until the review closes.
- Chat 68: instruments travel as bundle members; the gate fetches the two bundles from Drive by title; Drive is the store.
- Chat 69: handoff at 90–95 % or on a closed segment.
- Chat 70 (R1): CENSUS-CLOSURES-A governs its 21 shared rows; A vocabulary (*defect / not a defect*) in every closure file; an unreferenced prior-art row is a defect; co-located stale text counts against its census row.
- Chat 72: begin the close when the remaining context would not fit a segment plus the build; record the estimate.
- Chat 74: (1) no direct bundle uploads — Drive remains the store; (2) the gate and the close are instruments (gate.py, close.py, r2lib.py, banked NAME.out goldens); (3) the handoff carries identity, bootstrap, run list, next work, Drive actions and the prompt; rulings live in RULINGS-R2.md and deferred items in DEFERRED.md.
- M's priorities: the computational audits are paramount; every stated value is recomputed; stale self-description and production classes are noted, not a concern.
- Earlier rulings still governing the books: Ruling 29 (the only Register edit class: pointer removal), 38 (the Register's front matter is a purpose statement only), 41 (false carried state is discarded without refutation), 45 (no build or editorial-process remarks in any reader-facing volume), 46 (no script names, build numbers or internal file references visible to readers), 56 (Prints & Proofs as original-input witness), W-101 (all subject matter completely true and proven).

## 5. Standing discipline (gates G0…)

- **Measure from files, never recite.** Grep every line number before it is written. Label every claim MEASURED (with the command), INFERRED, or record-carried; inferences are never carried into a handoff as fact.
- **No silent change.** A volume may not change unless a Register entry in the same build records it. Every edit is a measured diff with count-asserted substitutions and a reverse-md5 guard; build.py's SUBS six-way split is the preferred discriminator (G0x).
- **Register entries are append-only** — never removed, relocated or renumbered; a superseded entry is corrected by a new entry that cites it; both states are preserved. Moving an entry out is a deletion.
- **When a reconstruction disagrees with the record, the finding is about the reconstruction.** Never withdraw a recorded finding on reconstructed evidence without the original instrument. Never change an instrument to make a discrepancy disappear (G0c).
- **Authorised work is reported done or not done;** a shortfall is named explicitly. Silence is not completion.
- A message containing a question ends at the question mark; the next action is never announced in the same message as a question (G0, highest priority). Rulings are compact numbered lists and take effect without re-explanation.
- A defect line and its disposition are different objects; the later line governs (G0b). Re-test defects from the file, never from prior dispositions. Measure in the pressed PDF, not simulation (G0aa); census figures at press, not at source (G0w). A docket's target is a hypothesis until read and measured (G0v).
- A command that deletes does nothing else (G0e). Never hand-transcribe base64. `validate=True` on every b64decode. Simulate sweep order before asserting anchor uniqueness (G0q). "Registers N" cites and is counted by register_cites.py; "entries N" merely names (G0i).
- `timeout 280` on every call. Never copy over an existing file; list a directory before copying. Never edit a seated member in place (append-only members grow only through close.py `--append`). Remove `members/__pycache__` (delete-only call) before any census or build and after every instrument run.
- Shell is dash: text goes through python heredocs or create_file; no `<(…)`; one heredoc per call; non-ASCII grep output through python. Import tower-2.py by path via r2lib.load_tower(), never by copying.
- Instruments print no wall-clock time (goldens must be deterministic); an instrument over ~200 s is trimmed. Functions owed to r2lib are copied verbatim into the new instrument with a provenance comment until lifted (DEFERRED lists them).
- C7/C9 census rows whose flagged token is a live figure, label, or the cited section's own claim are regex artefacts (precedents 678, 680–687, 1067, 1069).

## 6. Session shape

1. **§0 gate**, each step its own call: list directories; `recent_chats` confirms the latest chat; fetch both bundles by title (`title contains 'BUILDNNN_compendia' or title contains 'BUILD90_main'`, pageSize 5, excludeContentSnippets); bootstrap from the spill files with the handoff's script (assert md5s; extract members); `gate.py census`; `gate.py run --core`; `gate.py manifest`; `gate.py run` on the previous chat's instruments; `gate.py cert NN`. Any FAIL stops the chat with a report.
2. Read RULINGS-R2.md and DEFERRED.md from the members.
3. **Segments:** one or two subsections each. `r2-tools.py lines|pointers|figures|census|layout A B` (pointer regex is case-sensitive and ignores Appendix A item numbers — grep lowercase `register NNN` and `A.N` by hand); read every line; resolve every pointer to heading AND claim; grep every figure; re-measure every tower-computable claim on all cells or pairs in `members/r2-chNN.py` importing r2lib by path; write READ-chNN.md (A deviations with both texts; B verified; C incidental) and CENSUS-CLOSURES-chNN.tsv (id, verdict, reason; header only when no row is in range); bank the golden with `gate.py bank`.
4. **Close:** W-NNN.md (begins `### W-NNN —`, ends with a blank line; gate, segments, close estimate); `close.py --old … --new … --w … [--append DEFERRED.md …] --members …` (reverse must recover the old md5); HANDOFF-NN+1 in the current handoff's form; copy to outputs without overwriting; present the handoff first, then the build and the READ files; closing report of done / not done / M's Drive actions.

## 7. Content standards for the books

- All subject matter completely true and proven; every figure computed on the rebuilt lattice before authoring.
- Compendium entries follow R-FORM: descriptive title → bold dense headline with §-pointers on first mention → italic scope-caps line → Proved/Computed + citation chain → blockquote Prior art. All attributions that can be made are made (R-ATTR).
- No object handles or workshop jargon in reader-facing volumes; cross-references name the object by its descriptive title with a source pointer on first mention per entry. Image captions state facts only.
- The compendium standard: comprehensive scope without filler; intuitive taxonomy with a robust index; consistent formatting; concise synthesis; unified voice; strict fact-checking; fluid cross-referencing; dual-purpose accessibility; clear visual hierarchy. Compendium canon order is the main volume's physical order; reordering and renumbering is a last step executed once after all subject matter is settled.
- kinds.py's table is recomputed after any Register entry addition; extent ("1 to NNNN") restated everywhere.

## 8. Response style

- Focused and brief; caveats short; the bulk of the response is the answer; high-level unless depth was requested. Cover the substance; skip boilerplate and redundant summaries.
- Scope rule: deliver what was asked; raise a better approach in one sentence; then proceed as asked.
- Delegation rule: large independent work only, never for self-verification, low spawn counts.
- Keep internal or system tags out of responses. Rulings are given back as numbered lists.

## 9. Tools and quirks

- Drive: large files spill to `/mnt/user-data/tool_results/<id>.json`; decode with `base64.b64decode(json.loads(json.load(open(p))[0]['text'])['content'], validate=True)`. Small files arrive inline (quoted heredoc, strip, same decode). Hard cap ≈ 10 MB. `read_file_content` mangles indentation — never for code. `parentId = '<id>'` with excludeContentSnippets lists a folder.
- Bundle member extraction: `^<<<FILE: (.+?)>>>\n(.*?)<<<END FILE: \1>>>\n` with `re.S|re.M` on the decoded bytes; members of both bundles into one `/home/claude/members/`.
- Build pipeline: Markdown → pandoc → LibreOffice → docx/pdf; `pdftotext -layout` drops table rows — confirm through docx XML.

8964  A closed index admits nothing it lacks, so a *closed* index names nothing unidentified. **This book is
8965  not one index but six, and only two of them are closed.** Asked what it can determine before an input
8966  is given, the answer is a count:

8968   index                            coordinates   E     cells named and unoccupied
8969   Λ, the object                              8   0     —
8970   Appendix D, fibred by kind × language     16   0     —
8971   Appendix D, unfibred                       3   4     four
8972   Appendix E (Q), fibred by domain           4   0     —
8973   Appendix E (Q), unfibred                   4   1     one
8974   Appendix F, the numbers                    3  33     thirty-three
8975   the audit set, at four coordinates         4  17     seventeen
8976                                                        **a build readout**
8977 
8978  **Fifty-five cells are named and nobody has put anything in them.** Each is a combination the
8979  structure admits, stated in coordinates already defined, arrived at by computation and not by
8980  suggestion. That is what E(X) *is* — §18.6 calls it the prediction budget, and this is the budget
8981  unspent.
8982 
8983  **It has been confirmed three times, which is the only evidence that matters here.** Register 285:
8984  audit 19 SEQUENCE occupied a cell E(audits) had listed as admitted and absent, found by a defect
8985  rather than proposed. Register 294: PROJECTION did the same. Register 278: E over the book's own
8986  decisions located a decision that had been deferred rather than made — the section-level locators for
8987  Appendices B and F (then C and G). **In each case the cell was named first and the occupant arrived after.**
8988 
8989  **And there is a hard boundary, which is the honest half of the answer.** E names cells; it never
8990  names a coordinate. Every one of the fifty-five is a combination of values the index already carries,
8991  and §17's extension test requires a candidate axis to be *offered* before it can be judged. The book
8992  predicted the eleven missing audits and could not have predicted DEPTH, the coordinate that made them
8993  nineteen. **An index can tell you what it has not said in the language it has. It cannot tell you what
8994  it has no language for**, and that is §22.4's closing result read forward rather than back. Register
8995  332.
8996 
8997 ### 32.1.4.1 Which of this book's numbers hold still
8998  §32.1.4 counts fifty-five cells named and unoccupied. **Recomputed now the total is 48**, and the
8999  movement is the finding rather than the correction.

9002  register was compressed, and now:

9016  text that changes**, so a measurement of Λ is a measurement and a measurement of the book is a reading
9017  taken at a moment. §12.11.3.1 divides bounds into those from a law and those from an extent; the same
9018  division sorts this book's own numbers, and **the sorting line falls exactly at the boundary between
9019  the object and the work about it.**

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""r2-ch16m --- chat 121 --- COMPUTABLE batch for main L8889-L9029
(section 32.1.2 'Four of the seven', 32.1.3 'The frame has changed', 32.1.4 'What this book names',
32.1.4.1 'Which of this book's numbers hold still').

Discipline: r2lib imported BY PATH, nothing copied except the functions DEFERRED still records as
owed (body_range, provenance chat 108; last_md_heading and lettered_heading, provenance chat 118;
regentry and stemlines, written here and now owed to r2lib).  Resolvers take the LINE LIST.
Members are read, never a BUILDnnn bundle.  No wall-clock time is printed.  Decimal.quantize with a
named convention, never round().  L8_at returns 8-tuples whose index 1 is l, not 2.
"""
import re, sys, importlib.util
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP, ROUND_HALF_EVEN, ROUND_DOWN

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('r2lib', '/home/claude/members/r2lib.py')
r2lib = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(r2lib)
from r2lib import heading_line, section_span, has_token, enclosing, Rset, L8_at  # noqa: E402

VOL = {'main': 'The_Method_1_6-2.md', 'reg': 'The_Method_1_6___The_Register-2.md',
       'mc': 'The_Method_1_6___Mathematical_Compendium-2.md',
       'pc': 'The_Method_1_6___The_Physics_Compendium-2.md',
       'ioi': 'The_Method_1_6___The_Index_of_Indices-2.md',
       'sc': 'The_Method_1_6___Spectra_Compendium-2.md'}
V = {k: open('/home/claude/members/' + v, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n') for k, v in VOL.items()}
M = V['main']; R = V['reg']
U0, U1 = 8889, 9029                     # the unit, measured by heading scan in this chat
UNIT = M[U0 - 1:U1]

out = []
def p(*a): out.append(' '.join(str(x) for x in a))


def body_range(Mx, sec):
    """[start, end) of a section's OWN body.  Owed to r2lib; provenance chat 108."""
    s = heading_line(Mx, sec)
    if s is None:
        return None
    for i in range(s + 1, len(Mx) + 1):
        if re.match(r'^#{1,4} ', Mx[i - 1].strip()):
            return (s, i)
    return (s, len(Mx) + 1)


def lettered_heading(Mx, label):
    """Provenance chat 118; owed to r2lib.  Numeric patterns walk past '### F.4.3'."""
    hits = [i for i, t in enumerate(Mx, 1)
            if re.match(r'^#{1,4}\s+' + re.escape(label) + r'[ .]', t.strip())]
    return hits[-1] if hits else None


def regentry(Rx, n):
    """Grouped-aware Register lookup.  Entry headings are BARE numbers ('### 96'), so
    heading_line returns None for every one of them; a grouped heading ('### 96-98', '### 96, 97')
    covers each number it spans.  Existence FIRST, headline second.  Owed to r2lib."""
    for i, t in enumerate(Rx, 1):
        m = re.match(r'^#{1,4}\s*([0-9][0-9,\s\u2013\u2014-]*)\s*$', t.strip())
        if not m:
            continue
        spanned = set()
        for part in re.split(r',\s*', m.group(1).strip()):
            g = re.match(r'^(\d+)\s*[\u2013\u2014-]\s*(\d+)$', part.strip())
            if g:
                spanned |= set(range(int(g.group(1)), int(g.group(2)) + 1))
            elif part.strip().isdigit():
                spanned.add(int(part.strip()))
        if n in spanned:
            head = ''
            for j in range(i + 1, min(i + 6, len(Rx) + 1)):
                if Rx[j - 1].strip():
                    head = Rx[j - 1].strip(); break
            return (i, t.strip(), head)
    return None


def stemlines(Mx, stem, lo=1, hi=None):
    """Left-bounded stem matcher: has_token is letter-bounded on BOTH sides, so it cannot see a
    stem inside its own inflections.  Owed to r2lib."""
    hi = hi or len(Mx)

  f'computed over TWENTY-FIVE chapters')

  f'{"EXACT" if Decimal(26)/Decimal(4) == Decimal("6.5") else "DEVIATION"}')
p(f'  exact ratio (18/68)/(1/25) = {(Decimal(18)/Decimal(68))/(Decimal(1)/Decimal(25)):.4f}')

  f'{"EXACT" if Decimal(25)/Decimal(5) == 5 else "DEVIATION"};  "fall from 88% to 55%" printed and matches the table')

p('  32.1.4 table, L8968-L8976:')
E14 = [('Lambda, the object', 8, 0), ('App D fibred', 16, 0), ('App D unfibred', 3, 4),

closed = [n for n, _, e in E14 if e == 0]
p(f'      rows with E = 0 (closed): {len(closed)} {closed}')

  f'Lambda only = 1, against L8965 "only two of them are closed"')

p('  32.1.4.1 table, L9004-L9011, and the recomputation:')
now = {'App D unfibred': 4, 'App E(Q) unfibred': 4, 'App F numbers': 23, 'audit set': 17}
p(f'      "now" column recomputation {" + ".join(str(v) for v in now.values())} = {sum(now.values())}'

bok_rows = [('elements of App D', ['forty', 'forty-eight', 'forty-eight']),
            ('E over numbers', ['33', '21', '23']), ('E(Q) unfibred', ['1', '1', '4'])]
p(f'      L9013 "Every figure about Lambda holds": '

p(f'      main member {len(M):,} lines / {mb:,} B;  Register member {len(R):,} lines / {rb:,} B')
p(f'      Register as a share of main+Register: lines {pct(len(R), len(R)+len(M))[0]} %, '
  f'bytes {pct(rb, rb+mb)[0]} % (half-up);  as a share of main alone: '
  f'lines {pct(len(R), len(M))[0]} %, bytes {pct(rb, mb)[0]} %')

for phrase in ('twenty-two audits', 'twenty audits', 'nineteen audits', 'eleven missing audits',
               'all twenty audits'):

    p(f'      "{phrase}": {len(hits)} sites {hits[:8]}')

for phrase in ('companion paper', 'companion papers'):
    hits = [i for i, t in enumerate(M, 1) if phrase in t]

         and re.search(r'generator', t, re.I)]
    p(f'      {tag}: 7.07 at {a[:8]} ({len(a)});  "17 ... generator" at {b[:8]} ({len(b)})')

for phrase in ('forty-eight', 'forty eight'):

    p(f'      "{phrase}" in main at {hits[:12]} ({len(hits)})')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""r2-ch16n --- chat 121 --- PROSE batch for main L8889-L9029.

Same discipline as r2-ch16m: r2lib by path, resolvers take the LINE LIST, members never a bundle,
no wall-clock time.  Every negative states what the sweep covered.  Symbols are tested RAW.
A probe scoring zero on its own volume is a broken probe, not a finding.
"""
import re, sys, importlib.util

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('r2lib', '/home/claude/members/r2lib.py')
r2lib = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(r2lib)
from r2lib import heading_line, section_span, has_token, enclosing  # noqa: E402

VOL = {'main': 'The_Method_1_6-2.md', 'reg': 'The_Method_1_6___The_Register-2.md',
       'mc': 'The_Method_1_6___Mathematical_Compendium-2.md',
       'pc': 'The_Method_1_6___The_Physics_Compendium-2.md',
       'ioi': 'The_Method_1_6___The_Index_of_Indices-2.md',
       'sc': 'The_Method_1_6___Spectra_Compendium-2.md'}
V = {k: open('/home/claude/members/' + v, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n') for k, v in VOL.items()}
M = V['main']
PP = open('/home/claude/PP_The_Method_1_6.md', encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
U0, U1 = 8889, 9029
out = []
def p(*a): out.append(' '.join(str(x) for x in a))


def body_range(Mx, sec):                      # owed to r2lib; provenance chat 108
    s = heading_line(Mx, sec)
    if s is None:
        return None
    for i in range(s + 1, len(Mx) + 1):
        if re.match(r'^#{1,4} ', Mx[i - 1].strip()):
            return (s, i)
    return (s, len(Mx) + 1)


def lettered_heading(Mx, label):              # owed to r2lib; provenance chat 118
    hits = [i for i, t in enumerate(Mx, 1)
            if re.match(r'^#{1,4}\s+' + re.escape(label) + r'[ .]', t.strip())]
    return hits[-1] if hits else None


def last_md_heading(Mx, title):               # owed to r2lib; the BODY occurrence
    hits = [i for i, t in enumerate(Mx, 1)
            if re.match(r'^#{1,4}\s+' + re.escape(title) + r'\s*$', t.strip())]
    return hits[-1] if hits else None


def numsites(Mx, n, lo=1, hi=None):
    """Digit-bounded numeral SITE lister --- sites, never a count.  A figure spelled in words is
    invisible to it, so the word form is swept separately.  Owed to r2lib."""
    hi = hi or len(Mx)
    pat = re.compile(r'(?<![\d.,])' + str(n) + r'(?!\d)(?!,\d)(?!\.\d)')
    return [i for i in range(lo, hi + 1) if pat.search(Mx[i - 1])]


# ============================================================ A. pointers, both resolvers
p('== A. every pointer the unit makes, resolved under body_range AND section_span ==')
for sec in ('32.2', '18.6', '17', '22.4', '12.11.3.1', '32.1.4', '18.4.1'):
    br, ss = body_range(M, sec), section_span(M, sec)
    same = 'COINCIDE' if br == ss else 'DIFFER'
    p(f'  §{sec}: body_range {br}  section_span {ss}  {same}')
for lab in ('F.4.1', 'F.4.3'):
    h = lettered_heading(M, lab)
    p(f'  §{lab}: lettered_heading L{h}' + (f'  "{M[h-1].strip()[:80]}"' if h else '  ABSENT'))

p('  --- §32.2 read IN FULL (the S3 claim L8921-22 attributes to it):')
b322 = body_range(M, '32.2')
for i in range(b322[0], b322[1]):
    p(f'      L{i}: {M[i-1].strip()[:150]}')

p('  --- §18.6, the sentence L8980 attributes to it ("calls it the prediction budget"):')
b186 = body_range(M, '18.6')
hits = [i for i in range(b186[0], b186[1]) if re.search(r'budget', M[i - 1], re.I)]
p(f'      body {b186}; "budget" at {hits}')
for i in hits[:4]:
    p(f'      L{i}: {M[i-1].strip()[:150]}')
p(f'      "prediction budget" anywhere in main: {[i for i,t in enumerate(M,1) if "prediction budget" in t.lower()]}')

p('  --- §17\'s extension test, the requirement L8991 attributes to it ("a candidate axis offered"):')
s17 = section_span(M, '17')
p(f'      section_span(17) {s17}; body_range(17) {body_range(M, "17")}')
for probe in ('offer', 'candidate', 'extension test', 'axis'):
    h = [i for i in range(s17[0], s17[1]) if re.search(r'(?<![A-Za-z])' + probe, M[i - 1], re.I)]
    p(f'      "{probe}" in §17 span: {len(h)} sites {h[:10]}')

p('  --- §22.4\'s closing result, cited at L8994:')
b224 = section_span(M, '22.4')
p(f'      section_span(22.4) {b224}; last two non-blank body lines:')
nb = [i for i in range(b224[0], b224[1]) if M[i - 1].strip()]
for i in nb[-2:]:
    p(f'      L{i}: {M[i-1].strip()[:150]}')

p('  --- §12.11.3.1\'s division of bounds, cited at L9017:')
b12 = section_span(M, '12.11.3.1')
p(f'      section_span {b12}')
h = [i for i in range(b12[0], b12[1]) if re.search(r'(?<![A-Za-z])(law|extent)(?![A-Za-z])', M[i - 1], re.I)]
p(f'      "law"/"extent" at {h[:10]} ({len(h)})')
for i in h[:3]:
    p(f'      L{i}: {M[i-1].strip()[:150]}')

p('  --- part labels (parts carry NO markdown heading; the printed label is swept instead):')
plab = [(i, M[i - 1].strip()[:60]) for i, t in enumerate(M, 1) if re.match(r'^#*\s*PART\b', t.strip())]
p(f'      {len(plab)} PART labels: {[i for i,_ in plab]}')
for i, t in plab:
    p(f'      L{i}: {t}')
p(f'      L8958 "register 321 promoted the procedure to PART I" --- PART I above is the test')
p(f'      L8957 "Part VI carries the record" and L9021 "Parts II and III" resolve against that list')

# ============================================================ B. Ruling 45 / 46
p('')
p('== B. Ruling 45 (build and editorial-process narration) and Ruling 46 (script, build, file names) ==')
R45 = ['this build', 'the press', 'at every build', 'the session', 'these sessions', 'was written',
       'recomputed now', 'compressed', 'from here', 'this section was written', 'intake',
       'the book now prints', 'stopped being hidden', 'the book will track']
seen45 = {}
for i in range(U0, U1 + 1):
    for t in R45:
        if t in M[i - 1].lower():
            seen45.setdefault(i, []).append(t)
p(f'  Ruling 45 candidate sites in the unit: {len(seen45)}')
for i in sorted(seen45):
    p(f'      L{i} [{", ".join(seen45[i])}]: {M[i-1].strip()[:120]}')
R46 = re.compile(r'\b[a-z0-9_]+\.py\b|\bBUILD\d+\b|\bgate\.py\b|\bclose\.py\b|MANIFEST|\.tsv\b|\.md\b')
h46 = [(i, R46.findall(M[i - 1])) for i in range(U0, U1 + 1) if R46.search(M[i - 1])]
p(f'  Ruling 46 sites in the unit (case-sensitive): {len(h46)} {h46}')
p(f'      sweep covered every line L{U0}-L{U1} for .py, BUILD<n>, MANIFEST, .tsv and .md tokens')

# ============================================================ C. spliced text
p('')
p('== C. the spliced-text class (DEFERRED item 26) at L8908-L8912 ==')
for i in range(8908, 8913):
    p(f'      L{i}: {M[i-1].rstrip()}')
joined = ' '.join(M[i - 1].strip() for i in range(8909, 8912))
p(f'  two-line join L8909-L8911: "{joined[:220]}"')
p(f'  "= 0 at one fibre" occurrences in the join: {joined.count("= 0 at one fibre")}')
p(f'  line-length profile of the unit (chars): '
  f'{[len(M[i-1]) for i in range(8908, 8913)]} --- L8910 is short where its neighbours run long')

# ============================================================ D. count words, N-of-M, universals
p('')
p('== D. count words, N-of-M forms and list-opening universals, each against its own body ==')
CW = ['four', 'seven', 'three', 'six', 'two', 'eight', 'fifty-five', 'forty-two', 'thirty-four',
      'nineteen', 'twenty', 'eleven', 'forty-eight', 'nineteenth', 'twentieth']
for w in CW:
    h = [i for i in range(U0, U1 + 1) if has_token(M[i - 1], w)]
    if h:
        p(f'  "{w}": {h}')
p('  N-of-M forms in the unit:')
for i in range(U0, U1 + 1):
    for m in re.finditer(r'\b(\w+)\s+of\s+(?:the\s+)?(\w+[\w-]*)\b', M[i - 1]):
        if re.match(r'^(one|two|three|four|five|six|seven|eight|nine|ten|eleven|twelve|\d+)$',
                    m.group(1), re.I):
            p(f'      L{i}: "{m.group(0)}"  in: {M[i-1].strip()[:110]}')
p('  universals in the unit ("every", "each", "all", "nothing", "never", "only"):')
for i in range(U0, U1 + 1):
    for w in ('every', 'each', 'all', 'nothing', 'never', 'only'):
        if has_token(M[i - 1], w):
            p(f'      L{i} [{w}]: {M[i-1].strip()[:120]}')

# ============================================================ E. numeral sites

p('== E. digit-bounded numeral SITES for every figure the unit prints (sites, not counts) ==')
FIG = ['976', '8,853', '89,438', '267,858', '499,246', '18', '68', '26', '4', '42', '34', '8',

# READ-ch16o — chat 121 — main L8889–L9029 (§32.1.2, §32.1.3, §32.1.4, §32.1.4.1)

Unit cut by heading scan taken in this chat: §32.1.2 L8889, §32.1.3 L8933, §32.1.4 L8963,
§32.1.4.1 L8997, §32.2 L9030. The movement is read whole and closes where §32.2 begins.
141 lines. Instruments: `r2-ch16m` (computable, golden 11,481 B md5 d4755b1b, 129 lines) and
`r2-ch16n` (prose, golden 19,953 B md5 d2ef24a2, 235 lines). Every figure below is MEASURED at the
member unless marked INFERRED. No corrections and no Register entries: the chat-67 hold stands and
the chat-95 ruling governs — a finding is recorded and flagged for repair, never put to M.

## A. Deviations

**16o-01 — an S3 baseline computed over twenty-five chapters where the volume carries thirty-six.**
L8923–24 prints *18 of 68 — 26% against a 4% baseline from uniform guessing over twenty-five
chapters*, and L8924 concludes *six and a half times chance*. MEASURED: 18/68 = 26.4706 %, which is
26 under half-up, half-even AND truncation — the printed 26 is exact under every convention. The
baseline 1/25 = 4 % is exact for twenty-five chapters. But the volume's own `## N.` headings carry
**36 distinct chapter numbers, maximum 36** (70 heading lines, contents plus body). Against the book
as it stands the baseline is 1/36 = 2.78 % and the multiple is **9.53×, not 6.5×**. The stale
denominator *understates the book's own result*; the direction is the opposite of 16m-01's. Same
class as 16m-01: a figure computed from the book's own size is a measurement that goes stale.
Register 237 carries the 26 % at its headline and is not itself wrong.

**16o-02 — two of three table rows sum to a total three rounded percentages cannot reach.** The
§32.1.3 table L8939–L8941 partitions how defects were found into three columns. MEASURED sums:
L8939 (88, 5, 6) = **99**; L8940 (73, 23, 2) = **98**; L8941 (55, 25, 18) = **98**. Three values each
rounded to an integer from a partition summing to 100 must give a total in [98.5, 101.5], i.e. 99,
100 or 101. **99 is rounding-consistent; 98 is arithmetically impossible.** Two rows of three fail.
The prose drawn from the table (L8943, *88 % to 55 %* and *rise fivefold*, 5 → 25) is exact.

**16o-03 — a count word and a closure count that match neither reading of the section's own table.**
L8964–65: *This book is not one index but six, and only two of them are closed*, followed by the
table at L8968–L8976. MEASURED: the table has **7 rows** naming **5 distinct indices** — Λ, Appendix
D, Appendix E(Q), Appendix F, the audit set (D and E each appear twice, fibred and unfibred).
*Six* matches neither 7 nor 5. Closed rows (E = 0) number **3** under the fibred reading (Λ, App D
fibred, App E fibred) and **1** under the rule the section itself states sixty lines earlier at L8908
(*the honest number for a fibred index is its unfibred one*), which leaves only Λ. *Two* matches
neither. Both readings are recorded; neither is chosen here.

**16o-04 — "the register is a quarter of it" against a measured third to three fifths.** L8957.
MEASURED at the members: main `The_Method_1_6-2.md` **11,855 lines / 764,464 B**; Register
`The_Method_1_6___The_Register-2.md` **6,612 lines / 1,185,386 B**. The Register's share of main +
Register is **35.8 % by lines and 60.8 % by bytes** (half-up); as a share of the main volume alone,
55.8 % by lines and 155.1 % by bytes. Basis named: text lines and bytes at the members. A page-count
basis is not measurable in this container (no pressed PDF; G0aa makes the press the arbiter for a
page claim), but *a quarter* fails by a wide margin on both text bases. Docket 30's neighbourhood.

**16o-05 — two companion papers against the volume's own third.** L8945: *The third column is the
two companion papers — the method applied to electromagnetism and to muon-catalysed fusion*.
MEASURED across the main volume: *companion papers* (plural) at **3 sites, L4175, L8945, L11853**;
*companion paper* (singular) at **19 sites**, including **L1338** (*the third companion paper's third
finding*) and **L9001**, fourteen lines below the flag, (*before the third companion paper's
intake*). Chapters 35 and 36 are the two absorbed papers (L9716 *The Löwdin solution*, L9892 *Three
bodies*). The volume therefore names three companion papers and twice says two. Docket 14 and
docket 15.

**16o-06 — §22.4 cited for a closing result it does not carry.** L8993–94: *An index can tell you
what it has not said in the language it has. It cannot tell you what it has no language for, and
that is §22.4's closing result read forward rather than back.* §22.4 READ IN FULL at its target
under **both** resolvers — body_range (6137, 6147), section_span (6137, 6167), which **DIFFER** —
is *The price of limit-freedom, computed*: bracketing δ rather than T, L = |δ′/δ″| = n/3,
V(δ) = V(T) = 4n/(3h), closing at §22.4.1 L6165 on a conditional choice computable per channel.
MEASURED: *language* has **zero sites** in the §22.4 span; *no language for* has **exactly one site
in the whole main volume — L8994 itself**. Where the claim lives: nowhere else. Third member of
16m-05's shape (16j-02, 16m-05, 16o-06); docket 9(b).

**16o-07 — a corrupt sentence carrying the fibred/unfibred figures.** L8908–L8912 reads: *The honest
number for a fibred / index is its unfibred one. E(Appendix D) = 4 at one fibre, E(Q) unfibred as the
press reports it at each build, / E(Λ) = 0 at one fibre = 0 at one / fibre.* MEASURED: the phrase
*= 0 at one fibre* occurs **twice** in the two-line join; L8910 is **33 characters** where its four
neighbours run 98, 112, 101 and 79. Three defects in one sentence: (a) the duplication; (b) the
E(Q) clause carries **no number at all**; (c) *E(Appendix D) = 4 at one fibre* is unreadable against
§32.1.4's own table sixty lines later, which gives App D **fibred E = 0 and unfibred E = 4** — under
the reading *4 [unfibred], 0 at one fibre* the figures agree with the table, under the reading as
printed they contradict it, and the sentence does not disambiguate. PP: the L8908 witness anchors at
**P8814, offset −94** — the splice is in the original. Docket 26 and docket 14.

**16o-08 — the audit set at three counts, two of them narrated as past states without a marker.**
MEASURED across the main volume: *twenty-two audits* at **4 sites (L79, L1004, L1399, L9824)*;
*twenty audits* at **1 site — L8949, inside this unit**; *nineteen audits* at **0 sites**, the count
carried in prose at L8992–93 (*the eleven missing audits … the coordinate that made them nineteen*,
1 site). Registers 285 and 294 headline *A NINETEENTH PRIME AUDIT, SEQUENCE* and *A TWENTIETH PRIME
AUDIT, PROJECTION*, so nineteen and twenty are successive past states and the unit's prose is
internally coherent as narration; twenty-two is the volume's present. The unit prints two superseded
counts with no state marker, in a section whose whole subject is that figures about the book are true
of a state. Docket 33 and docket 15.

## B. Verified findings

1. **The enlargement table is exact in every row.** L8895–L8900 printed against `L8_at` measured:
   (3,3,1,3,1) **976**, (4,4,1,6,1) **8,853**, (5,5,2,10,2) **89,438**, (5,5,3,14,3) **267,858**,
   (6,6,3,14,3) **499,246** — all EXACT. |ℛ(Λ)| = |Λ| and **E = 0** measured exactly at the first
   three rows; the last two are **not computed** because the ambient box is 18,900,000 and 27,216,000
   cells against a stated 4,000,000-cell budget. That is a budget bound, **not** a negative finding.
   Register 236's headline carries the same figures (*E(Λ) = 0 at 8,853 cells, 89,438 with d, and
   267,858 …*).
2. The shell labels are exact: ℓ ∈ {0,1} at *s, p*; {0,1,2} at *+ d*; {0,1,2,3} at *+ f*; n ≤ 6 at
   the last row. (ℓ is tuple index **1**, chat 120's fault, not repeated.)
3. **The count word chat 120 opened resolves as a pass on the successor.** §32.1.1's body carries
   **12 bolded lead-ins: 3 ordinals (L8813, L8835, L8841), 7 numbered (L8848, L8860, L8865, L8871,
   L8876, L8881, L8885) and 2 that are table/prose lines, not flags (L8823, L8825)**. §32.1.2 answers
   flags **1, 2, 4, 6** and defers **3, 5, 7** at L8929 — together **exactly 1–7, no gap, no
   duplicate**. *Four of the seven* is exact against the numbered list. 16m-02 is confined to
   §32.1.1's two labelling conventions; the successor title is not a second member.
4. 34 + 8 = **42** exact against *forty-two*; the eight registers listed at L8916–17 are **eight**
   and **all eight exist** (203, 215, 218 in one grouped heading; 207, 213, 220, 221 in another;
   227 in a third).
5. 18/68 = **26 %** exact under half-up, half-even and truncation; 26/4 = **6.5** exact against *six
   and a half times chance*.
6. 5 → 25 is exactly **fivefold**; *88 % to 55 %* matches the table's own first column.
7. **4 + 1 + 33 + 17 = 55** exact against L8978 *Fifty-five*; **4 + 4 + 23 + 17 = 48** exact against
   L8998 *Recomputed now the total is 48*; the net −7 is exactly the two moved rows (E over the
   numbers 33 → 23, E(Q) 1 → 4).
8. **L9013's two universals hold row by row.** Λ's four rows are constant across all three states
   (E(Λ) 0/0/0, |Λ| 976/976/976, |J(Λ)| 17/17/17, surplus 7.07/7.07/7.07); the book's three rows all
